name: Mandarin Chinese
target: Near-native ambition - advanced Mandarin and written Chinese
intro: The main writing system is simplified Chinese with pinyin at the foundation stage. Learn traditional recognition for materials from Taiwan, Hong Kong and historical or regional publishing, without assuming all traditional-text communities speak Mandarin in the same way. Spoken Mandarin and formal written Chinese overlap but are not identical. Character knowledge, extensive reading and a broad lexicon are essential for the ambition you described.

foundation.name: Mandarin Chinese

letters.name: unrounded back vowel in many syllables
first, second, third, fourth, neutral tone

notes: Mandarin writing uses characters. Pinyin is a Roman-letter pronunciation notation, not the usual replacement for characters. Begin with both. This course uses simplified characters; traditional counterparts are a separate recognition extension.

An initial combines with a final and a tone: m + a + first tone → mā. Finals can contain more than one vowel or a nasal: ai, ei, ao, ou, an, en, ang, eng, ong. y/w often spell syllables with no consonantal initial. After j/q/x/y, written u normally represents ü.

mā 妈 = mother; má 麻 = hemp; mǎ 马 = horse; mà 骂 = scold. Third tone is often low without a full rise in connected speech; before another third tone it commonly becomes rising. 一 and 不 change tone in predictable contexts. Written pinyin usually shows citation tones; audio carries connected-speech changes.
building: 氵 often suggests water: 河 = river. A component may hint at meaning, pronunciation, both or neither clearly in modern use. Learn a character’s components without assuming a component guarantees its pronunciation.
学 = learn; 生 = life/birth; 学生 = student. 学校 = school; 大学 = university. A character can occur in many words; the word’s meaning is not always a literal sum.

Practise horizontal before vertical, left before right, and top before bottom as general guides. Enclosures have special sequences and exceptions. Check an actual stroke-order reference for each new character; these rules do not determine every stroke order.

Learn a component as a recognition aid: 氵 water; 亻 person; 扌 hand; 口 mouth; 心/忄 heart or feelings; 木 wood; 日 sun/day; 月 moon or flesh in different histories; 女 woman; 宀 roof; 艹 plants; 讠 speech; 钅 metal; 饣 food; 火/灬 fire; 土 earth; 足 foot; 目 eye; 耳 ear; 门 gate; 纟 silk/thread; 辶 movement; 贝 shell/money; 车 vehicle. A component is not a guaranteed definition, and the dictionary radical used for lookup can differ from the most memorable component.

sections.title: Pinyin, tones and character learning
sections.explanation:
Pinyin represents Mandarin sounds; English letter values are unreliable guides. The four lexical tones and neutral tone need audio practice. Third tone is frequently low in connected speech rather than a full isolated dip and rise. Before another third tone, the first commonly changes to a rising contour; spelling usually preserves the underlying third-tone marks. 一 and 不 have context-dependent tone changes.
Learn characters as meaningful components and words, not as arbitrary pictures. A radical helps classification and lookup; a phonetic component can suggest pronunciation imperfectly. 学, 学生 and 学习 should be learned as related but distinct entries. Stroke order generally follows top-to-bottom and left-to-right patterns with exceptions; use a reliable animated model when practising an unfamiliar character. Do not mistake knowledge of a character's English gloss for knowledge of every word containing it.
examples: 你好 nǐ hǎo
Hello.
The first underlying third tone is commonly realised with a rising contour before the second third tone.
学习 xuéxí / 学生 xuésheng
to study / student
Word boundaries and readings matter; components are not a complete translation method.
exercises: Why should pinyin be reduced gradually?
It can support pronunciation initially, but continuous dependence prevents fluent character recognition. Preserve it on vocabulary cards while reading simple native-script sentences.
Does a radical reliably determine the modern meaning and pronunciation?
No. Radicals are useful clues and indexing tools; historical development and sound change make many relationships imperfect.

sections.title: Sentence order, topic and omitted arguments
sections.explanation:
A basic sentence often follows subject + verb + object, but Mandarin frequently organises information as topic + comment. 这本书，我看过 presents the book as what the comment is about. A topic need not be the grammatical subject. Subjects and objects can be omitted when recoverable; identify their referents from discourse rather than inserting an English pronoun mechanically.
Time expressions usually precede the verb, and place expressions commonly appear before the main verb with 在. 是 identifies or classifies but is not inserted before every adjective. 很 often occurs before a simple adjectival predicate without necessarily meaning an emphatic very. Negation and questions interact with the predicate: 不 often negates habitual or general situations; 没 or 没有 denies occurrence or possession in appropriate contexts.
examples: 这本书，我已经看过了。 Zhè běn shū, wǒ yǐjīng kàn guo le.
I have already read this book.
The book is the topic; 过 marks experience and 了 contributes current relevance or a changed situation.
他今天在图书馆学习。 Tā jīntiān zài túshūguǎn xuéxí.
He is studying in the library today.
Time and location precede the lexical verb.
exercises: Correct the idea that 是 is required before every adjective.
她很忙 is a normal predicate: she is busy. 她是忙 requires a special contrastive context rather than functioning as a default translation of is.
Ask Have you read this book? using 过.
你看过这本书吗？ Nǐ kàn guo zhè běn shū ma? 过 asks about experience.

sections.title: Aspect: 了, 过, 着 and ongoing activity
sections.explanation:
Mandarin does not conjugate verbs for past tense. Aspect presents how a situation unfolds. Verb-suffix 了 often marks a bounded or completed event; sentence-final 了 often signals a changed situation or new relevance. They can coexist, and their interpretation depends on context. A sentence in the past does not automatically require 了.
过 marks experiential occurrence, 着 often a continuing state, and 在 or 正在 an ongoing action. 他坐着 describes a sitting posture; 他正在坐下 describes an action of sitting down. Negating an event often uses 没有 and omits event-perfective 了. Duration and result structures determine placement; avoid treating these particles as English tense endings.
examples: 我以前住在北京。 Wǒ yǐqián zhù zài Běijīng.
I used to live in Beijing.
以前 provides the past frame; no automatic past-tense suffix is needed.
门开着。 Mén kāi zhe.
The door is open.
着 presents a continuing state.
exercises: Distinguish 我看了这本书 and 我看过这本书.
The first presents reading as a bounded event in context; the second foregrounds having the experience of reading it. Neither maps mechanically to one English tense.
Negate 我买了票.
我没买票。 Wǒ méi mǎi piào. 没 negates the occurrence, and event-perfective 了 is normally absent.

sections.title: Classifiers, quantification and noun modification
sections.explanation:
A numeral or demonstrative normally combines with a classifier before a count noun: 一本书, 这位老师. 个 is widespread but is not a universal replacement in careful usage. Learn classifier-noun combinations and meaningful contrasts, such as a sheet, volume, unit or person. Measure expressions can quantify mass nouns.
的 commonly links modifiers to nouns. A relative-like modifier precedes the head noun: 我昨天买的书, the book I bought yesterday. Complex noun phrases can contain several layers; find the final head first. 的, 地 and 得 have distinct functions in standard writing: nominal modification, adverbial modification and complements after predicates. Contemporary usage and fixed expressions create exceptions; their shared pronunciation does not make them interchangeable.
examples: 我昨天买的那本书 Wǒ zuótiān mǎi de nà běn shū
that book I bought yesterday
The clause modifies the final noun; 那 + 本 identifies the book.
他认真地解释，解释得很清楚。 Tā rènzhēn de jiěshì, jiěshì de hěn qīngchu.
He explains carefully and makes the explanation clear.
地 marks adverbial manner; 得 introduces the degree/result-like complement.
exercises: Build three books with the common classifier for books.
三本书 sān běn shū. 本 classifies bound volumes.
Translate the method we used.
我们使用的方法 wǒmen shǐyòng de fāngfǎ. The modifying clause precedes 方法.

sections.title: Complements, 把 and 被
sections.explanation:
Result complements express the result of an action: 看懂 understand by reading, 写完 finish writing. Potential complements indicate whether that result can be achieved: 看得懂 / 看不懂. Direction complements can be spatial or extended metaphorically. Identify the whole verb-complement construction before translating.
把 places an affected, identifiable object before the verb and normally requires a predicate that says what happens to it, rather than a bare undifferentiated verb. 我把报告写完了 specifies completion. 被 introduces a passive perspective; negative effects are common but not obligatory. Passive and 把 sentences are discourse choices, not stylistic upgrades to every basic sentence.
examples: 这个句子我看不懂。 Zhège jùzi wǒ kàn bu dǒng.
I cannot understand this sentence by reading it.
Potential negative complement focuses on failure to achieve understanding.
请把结果写在这里。 Qǐng bǎ jiéguǒ xiě zài zhèlǐ.
Please write the results here.
把 foregrounds the affected object; location completes the predicate.
exercises: Express I finished reading the report.
我看完报告了。 Wǒ kàn wán bàogào le. 看完 supplies the completion result.
Why is 我把书看 usually incomplete as a neutral sentence?
A 把 predicate normally specifies an effect, result, location or comparable development. 我把书看完了 supplies the missing result.

sections.title: Comparison, condition and logical scope
sections.explanation:
比 introduces comparison: A 比 B 更清楚. 没有 can express being less than a comparator; 不比 does not assert a simple less-than relation in the same way. 越……越…… expresses a proportional relationship. Condition pairs include 如果……就……, 只要……就…… and 只有……才……; sufficient and necessary conditions are not equivalent.
Learn the scope of 都, 也, 只, 不 and other operators. 不都 means not all, while 都不 means all not or none, with context. Formal argument uses 虽然……但是…… for concession and 因为……所以…… for cause and consequence. English often avoids using both although and but in one structure, but paired Chinese connectors are conventional.
examples: 只有证据充分，才能得出结论。 Zhǐyǒu zhèngjù chōngfèn, cái néng déchū jiélùn.
Only with sufficient evidence can a conclusion be drawn.
只有 ... 才 presents a necessary condition.
这些结果不都可靠。 Zhèxiē jiéguǒ bù dōu kěkào.
Not all these results are reliable.
Negation scopes over the universal quantifier.
exercises: Contrast 只要 with 只有.
只要 typically introduces a sufficient condition; 只有 introduces a necessary condition followed by 才. Do not substitute one for the other mechanically.
Translate The more carefully we check, the easier it is to find errors.
我们检查得越仔细，就越容易发现错误。 Wǒmen jiǎnchá de yuè zǐxì, jiù yuè róngyì fāxiàn cuòwù. Other natural wordings are possible.

sections.title: Formal written Chinese and academic vocabulary
sections.explanation:
Formal written Chinese uses compact nominal expressions and discourse markers such as 然而, 因此, 此外 and 综上所述. 关于 introduces a topic concerning; 对于 frames a relation to a matter or participant; their distributions overlap but are not universally interchangeable. 所 structures and compact relative modification are frequent in formal prose. Classical Chinese is a separate long-term study area, not automatically mastered through modern Mandarin.
Common research terms include 研究 study, 方法 method, 结果 result, 证据 evidence, 假设 hypothesis, 结论 conclusion and 局限 limitation. Translation depends on domain: significant may be 重要 for importance or 显著 for statistical significance in context. Keep technical terms in collocations and check a specialist source.
examples: 现有证据尚不足以支持这一结论。 Xiànyǒu zhèngjù shàng bù zú yǐ zhīchí zhè yī jiélùn.
The current evidence is not yet sufficient to support this conclusion.
尚, 不足以 and 这一 contribute formal register and evidential limitation.
所采用的方法 suǒ cǎiyòng de fāngfǎ
the method adopted
所 + verb + 的 forms a formal modifying expression.
exercises: Distinguish 重要 from 显著 in a research context.
重要 concerns importance; 显著 can denote a marked difference or statistical significance. The latter does not automatically imply practical importance.
Write a cautious conclusion with 可能.
这些结果可能反映了样本之间的差异。 These results may reflect differences between samples. Preserve possibility rather than claiming proof.

sections.title: Advanced reading, pragmatics and revision
sections.explanation:
Original teaching passage: 一种解释即使听起来合理，也未必得到充分的证据支持。研究者不仅需要说明自己的假设如何解释观察结果，还需要考虑其他解释是否同样成立。因此，阅读研究报告时，应当区分数据本身、作者的推断以及尚未解决的问题。
Translation: Even if an explanation sounds reasonable, it is not necessarily supported by sufficient evidence. Researchers need not only explain how their hypothesis accounts for observations, but also consider whether other explanations are equally valid. Therefore, when reading a research report, one should distinguish the data themselves, the author's inferences and unresolved questions.
Notice the concession 即使 ... 也, the limitation 未必, the additive 不仅 ... 还 and the embedded 是否. In everyday communication, requests and refusals also depend on relationship and context. Politeness cannot be reduced to adding 请 before every sentence. Revise a translation for natural topic flow and conventional collocations, not just character-by-character fidelity.
examples: 未必得到充分的证据支持
not necessarily supported by sufficient evidence
未必 denies necessity, not every possibility of support.
尚未解决的问题
questions that have not yet been resolved
A pre-nominal modifier compresses the temporal qualification.
exercises: Identify three different objects of 区分 in the passage.
数据本身, 作者的推断 and 尚未解决的问题: data, author inference and unresolved questions.
Write a 100-character summary without repeating whole sentences.
Preserve the distinction between plausibility and evidence, include alternative explanations and avoid turning 未必 into an absolute denial. Use the guide's accuracy and coherence rubric.

rules.title: Personal pronouns
rules.pattern: (?:我|你|他|她|我们|你们|他们|她们)
rules.explanation: Mandarin pronouns do not conjugate a verb. 他 and 她 differ in writing but share spoken tā. Context can omit a known subject; omission is a discourse choice rather than a new verb ending.

examples.translation: They won't find Tom.
Come on, let's go.

examples.native: 你們要是用刀劍刺我們，我們不是也會出血嗎？
examples.translation: If you prick us, do we not bleed?

rules.title: Identity with 是
rules.explanation: 是 commonly links identity or classification. Ordinary adjectival predicates do not require 是 merely because English uses be. 是 also appears in focus constructions, so read the whole predicate.

examples.native: 莎士比亞是一位作家的名字。
examples.translation: Shakespeare is the name of a writer.

examples.native: 哪個比較重，鉛還是黃金？
examples.translation: Which is heavier, lead or gold?

examples.native: 勇气是一个奇怪的东西：没有任何人对它有把握
examples.translation: Courage is a strange thing: One can never be sure of it.

rules.title: Possession and existence 有
rules.explanation: 有 expresses possession or existence. Its common negation is 没有, not 不有. A location phrase can precede an existence statement to introduce a new referent.

examples.translation: Tom has Mary's address.

examples.native: 他的英文作文沒有甚麼錯處。
examples.translation: Errors are few, if any, in his English composition.

examples.native: 上海这个地方，海内海外什么菜肴都有。
examples.translation: Shanghai has everything under the sun when it comes to food.

rules.title: Location and ongoing 在
rules.explanation: 在 can locate an entity or precede a verb for an ongoing action. It also appears in pre-verbal location phrases. The following phrase and predicate determine its role.

examples.native: 实在抱歉，老板在睡觉。请您明天再来。
examples.translation: I'm sorry, my boss is sleeping right now. Please come back tomorrow.

examples.native: 汽车尾气在城镇里造成了严重的污染。
examples.translation: Car exhaust causes serious pollution in towns.

examples.native: 放在保險箱裏面的文件不見了。
examples.translation: The papers that were in the safe are gone.

rules.title: Negation 不 and 没
rules.explanation: 不 commonly negates habits, states and many intentions; 没/没有 commonly negates occurrence or possession. A completed-event 了 is normally not retained mechanically in a 没 negative.

examples.native: 你千萬不要和你父母說這件事。
examples.translation: You mustn't tell that to your parents.

examples.native: 汤姆不能告诉玛丽他知道的所有事。
examples.translation: Tom couldn't tell Mary everything he knew.

examples.native: 雖然肉比魚昂貴，但是兩者的營養價值其實是差不多的。
examples.translation: Fish and meat are both nourishing, but the latter is more expensive than the former.

rules.title: Attributive 的
rules.explanation: 的 commonly links a modifier to a noun and marks possession. Mandarin modifiers precede their head noun. The written homophones 的/地/得 have distinct conventional functions.

examples.native: 那个男孩子见到鬼的时候吓了一跳。
examples.translation: The boy fell of fright when he saw a ghost.

examples.native: 國際間的紛爭一定要用和平的方法來解決。
examples.translation: International disputes must be settled peacefully.
You should consult your doctor.

rules.title: Classifiers
rules.explanation: A numeral/demonstrative commonly combines with a classifier before a counted noun. 本 is common for books, 张 for flat objects, 位 for people respectfully. Classifier choice is lexical and meaning-dependent.

examples.translation: Tom has made a big mistake.

examples.native: 我们已经等了好几个小时了。
examples.translation: We’ve been waiting for hours.

examples.native: 求你了，给我一个瓶子吧！
examples.translation: I beg you, give me a bottle!

rules.title: Demonstratives
rules.explanation: Demonstratives distinguish near/far or discourse reference. Counted noun phrases usually include the appropriate classifier. 这/那 also occur in other constructions, so determine whether a noun phrase follows.

examples.native: 汤姆如果想通过这门课，就需要加劲学习。
examples.translation: Tom needs to study more if he hopes to pass this class.
The incident was etched in his memory.

examples.native: 那房子比他那座好得多了。
examples.translation: That house is much better than his house.

rules.title: Completion and change 了
rules.explanation: 了 can mark a completed/bounded event or a change of situation. Its position and surrounding structure matter. It is not a universal past-tense ending and can occur in future contexts.

examples.translation: Today, many problems were encountered.
I gave Tom one of those.
I've been looking for a new job for a long time.

rules.title: Experience 过
rules.explanation: Aspectual 过 indicates prior experience in suitable verb constructions. The same character can have lexical or complement uses. Negated experience commonly uses 没 ... 过.

examples.native: 今晚我将在朋友家过夜。
examples.translation: I will put up at my friend's tonight.
I haven't seen him for years.
When did you tell me?

rules.title: State 着
rules.explanation: Aspectual 着 often marks a maintained state or accompanying posture. It differs from pre-verbal 在 for a dynamic ongoing activity. Read its relation to the verb rather than treating every occurrence identically.

examples.translation: A fallen leaf floated on the surface of the water.
Tom tried to kill Mary.

examples.native: 中国的经济随着时间的推移而变得越来越好。
examples.translation: As time goes on, China's economy gets stronger and stronger.

rules.title: Disposal 把
rules.explanation: A 把 construction places a disposal-affected object before the verb. It commonly needs a suitably specific object and a predicate describing its handling/result. 把 is also a classifier in other contexts.

examples.native: 把椅子挪一挪靠近桌子。
examples.translation: Move the chair nearer to the desk.

examples.native: 可以把新地址告訴我嗎？
examples.translation: Please let me know your new address.

examples.native: 我保證在一個星期內把這盤錄影帶還給你。
examples.translation: I promise to return this videotape within a week.

rules.title: Passive 被
rules.explanation: 被 introduces a passive-like affected-participant construction. The agent can be expressed or omitted. Passive meaning does not automatically imply the same word order as English.

examples.native: 道路法规必须被严格遵守。
examples.translation: The rule of the road must be strictly observed.

examples.native: 人类登上月球、柏林墙倒下，世界被我们的科学和想像被连接在一起。
examples.translation: A man touched down on the moon. A wall came down in Berlin. A world was connected by our own science and imagination.

examples.native: 這本小說已被翻譯成多國語言。
examples.translation: The novel has been translated into many languages.

rules.title: Result and degree 得
rules.explanation: 得 can introduce degree/manner complements after a verb; it also occurs in potential and lexical constructions. A complement may require repeating a verb when an object is present.

examples.translation: Mary looks like her mother.
He returned very late at night.

examples.native: 女人往往比男人活得更長。
examples.translation: Women tend to live longer than men.

rules.title: Comparison 比
rules.explanation: 比 introduces a comparison standard. The adjective does not generally need 更 in the simplest pattern. Compare equality with 跟/和 ... 一样 rather than mechanically adding 比 to every comparison.

examples.native: 信濃川比日本的任何一條河川更長。
examples.translation: The Shinano River is longer than any river in Japan.

examples.native: 她的氣色看起來比以前好。
examples.translation: She looks better than before.

examples.native: 巧克力的鐵質含量比菠菜還要多。
examples.translation: Chocolate's iron content is higher than spinach's.

rules.title: Question particles
rules.explanation: 吗 commonly turns a statement into a yes/no question. 呢 can ask about a topic or continuation. Question-word questions ordinarily do not add 吗 merely because they are questions.

examples.translation: I'm sorry, could you say that again?

examples.native: 您想知道为什么我要离开吗？
examples.translation: Do you want to know why I quit?

examples.native: 我能用法语加一句句子吗？
examples.translation: Can I enter a sentence in French?

rules.title: Question words
rules.pattern: (?:什么|谁|哪|哪里|哪儿|为什么|怎么|多少|几)
rules.explanation: Mandarin question words commonly stay in the position of the unknown information. 谁 asks a person, 哪里 a place, and 几/多少 quantities. No English-style subject-auxiliary inversion is required.

examples.translation: Why are you worried about me?
What do you think should be done about it?
Tell me how to play the game.

rules.title: Conditions and concession
rules.pattern: (?:如果|要是|虽然|但是|可是|的话)
rules.explanation: 如果/要是 introduce conditions; 虽然 presents concession, often paired with 但是. 的话 can frame an if scenario. Connectors express relationships, not tense inflections.

examples.native: 虽然听起来很奇怪，但是她说的的确是真的。
examples.translation: Even though it sounds strange, what she said is true.

examples.native: 如果你想使他人相信你的话，那就只说他已经相信的东西吧。
examples.translation: If you want to be credible, tell people only what they believe.

examples.native: 根据你所说的话，我认为我们应该重新审视我们的计划。
examples.translation: In the light of what you told us, I think we should revise our plan.

rules.title: Cause and inference
rules.explanation: 因为 supplies a reason; 所以/因此 supply a consequence. 可能 limits certainty and 应该 can indicate expectation or obligation. Translate the force of the claim, not just the dictionary gloss.

examples.translation: You must know yourself.

examples.native: 因为下雨了，球场上没有很多观众。
examples.translation: There weren't many spectators at the game because of the rain.

examples.native: 她妈妈来自西班牙，她爸爸来自意大利，所以她会讲西班牙语和意大利语。
examples.translation: Her mom is from Spain and her dad is from Italy, that's why she can speak both Spanish and Italian.

rules.title: Ability and intention
rules.explanation: 会, 能 and 可以 differ in learned ability, possibility and permission, with overlap in context. 要 and 想 express different strengths of intention/desire. These words do not trigger verb conjugation.

examples.native: 這台相機至少要花費500美元。
examples.translation: The camera will cost at least $500.

examples.native: 步行到車站要花十分鐘。
examples.translation: It's ten minutes' walk to the station.
I thought I could be of some help.

questions.native: 他们不会找到汤姆。
questions.translation: They won't find Tom.
questions.explanation: Mandarin pronouns do not conjugate a verb. 他 and 她 differ in writing but share spoken tā. Context can omit a known subject; omission is a discourse choice rather than a new verb ending.

passages.title: Learning with a clear purpose
passages.native: 我在学习一门新的语言。每天，我读一篇短文，听一些清楚的例句。我把有用的词写在笔记本里。如果我犯了错误，我会查看语法规则，然后再试一次。我的目标是理解别人，并清楚地表达自己的想法。
passages.translation: I am learning a new language. Each day, I read a short text and listen to clear examples. I write useful words in a notebook. When I make a mistake, I check the rule and try again. My goal is to understand people and express my ideas clearly.

passages.title: Environment: making trade-offs explicit
passages.native: 保护环境的措施往往同时带来收益和成本。一项政策可能减少污染，却增加某些家庭的支出。讨论这类问题时，不能只问总收益是否大于总成本，还应当考虑哪些人获得收益，哪些人承担成本。不同地区的情况也可能不同。因此，合理的评估需要说明比较的范围、使用的数据以及尚未解决的不确定性。把这些条件说清楚，并不意味着反对环境保护，而是为了让选择更加透明。
passages.guide: Environmental measures often bring both benefits and costs. A policy may reduce pollution but increase some households' spending. Evaluation must consider not only total benefits and costs, but also who receives the benefits and bears the costs. Regional conditions can differ. A sound assessment states scope, evidence and unresolved uncertainty. Making these conditions explicit supports transparent choices rather than opposing environmental protection.

grammarTerms: Noun
A word naming a person, thing or idea: student, book, freedom.
Verb
A word describing an action or state: read, know, be.
Subject
The participant linked to the main verb’s subject pattern. In The student reads a book, the student is the subject.
Object
A participant selected by a verb. In The student reads a book, a book is the direct object.
Agreement
One word changes to match another, for example an adjective matching a noun’s gender and number.
Case
A noun/pronoun form marking its relationship in a sentence. Cases can mark subjects, objects, possession or relations usually expressed by English prepositions.
Gender
A grammatical noun class. It does not always describe the sex of a person or any physical property.
Tense
A verb system that relates a situation to a time, often past or non-past.
Aspect
How a situation is viewed: unfolding, completed, habitual, experienced or in a resulting state.
Infinitive
A non-finite verb form often used for a dictionary entry or a complement. It does not by itself give the ordinary person/tense pattern.
Participle
A verb-derived form used in compound predicates or as a modifier; its exact function depends on the language and construction.
Clause
A unit organised around a predicate. One sentence can contain several clauses.
Register
Language choices suited to a situation: casual conversation, polite requests, academic writing or another context.
